domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's leave application — the central aggregate of the leave management module. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, manager decision, and potential cancellation.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT: Employee is composing the request; not yet visible to managers. May be edited freely.
SUBMITTED: Employee has submitted for manager review. Visible to the employee's manager. Awaiting decision.
APPROVED: Manager has approved the request. Balance is deducted. Terminal positive state.
REJECTED: Manager has rejected the request. No balance impact. Terminal negative state.
CANCELLED: Request was cancelled — by employee (from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED) or administratively. If cancelled from APPROVED, balance is restored.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of all lifecycle states a LeaveRequest can occupy. Governs which transitions are legal.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT
SUBMITTED
APPROVED
REJECTED
CANCELLED

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Catalog of leave categories. Each LeaveRequest references one LeaveType. The code drives policy lookup and balance tracking.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: Leave type is available for employees to request.
INACTIVE: Leave type is disabled; no new requests accepted. Existing approved requests remain valid.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules governing a specific leave type: how many days are entitled, whether manager approval is required, minimum notice periods, and accrual behaviour. Referenced by LeaveBalance to compute remaining entitlement.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: Policy is in effect and governs new leave requests.
INACTIVE: Policy is retired; does not apply to new requests. Existing balances under this policy remain until year-end.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific policy and fiscal year. `pendingDays` captures days tied to SUBMITTED (not yet decided) requests; `usedDays` captures APPROVED days; `remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays - pendingDays`.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: Balance is the current, operative balance for the fiscal year.
CLOSED: Balance has been finalised at fiscal year-end. No further deductions or additions.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organisation. The managerId establishes the approval hierarchy: a LeaveRequest is routed to the employee's manager for decision. Employment status gates eligibility for new leave requests.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: Employee is currently employed and eligible for leave.
INACTIVE: Employee is on extended leave or suspended; leave requests may be restricted.
TERMINATED: Employment has ended. No new leave requests allowed. Historical balances preserved.

domain_entities.name: Notification
domain_entities.purpose: Domain event notification triggered by LeaveRequest lifecycle transitions. Notifies managers of new submissions and employees of decisions on their requests.
lifecycle_states: PENDING: Notification created but not yet delivered.
SENT: Notification has been delivered to the recipient.
READ: Recipient has acknowledged the notification.
ARCHIVED: Notification is no longer shown in the active inbox.

business_rules: Leave day count is always inclusive of both startDate and endDate. Formula: requestedDays = (endDate - startDate) + 1, where the difference is in calendar days. A single-day leave (startDate = endDate) consumes 1 day. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest day counting appears, not only here]

Legal state transitions for LeaveRequest: DRAFT → SUBMITTED (employee submits), DRAFT → CANCELLED (employee discards), SUBMITTED → APPROVED (manager approves), SUBMITTED → REJECTED (manager rejects), SUBMITTED → CANCELLED (employee withdraws), APPROVED → CANCELLED (employee or admin cancels). No other transitions are permitted. REJECTED is terminal; a rejected request cannot be resubmitted — a new LeaveRequest must be created. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest state transitions appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the requested day count and pendingDays is decremented by the same amount. When a LeaveRequest transitions to SUBMITTED, pendingDays is incremented by the requested day count. When a SUBMITTED request is REJECTED, pendingDays is decremented. When an APPROVED request is CANCELLED, usedDays is decremented (balance restored). DRAFT requests have no balance impact. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance deduction appears, not only here]

Before a LeaveRequest can transition from DRAFT to SUBMITTED, the system must verify that remainingDays (after accounting for pendingDays) is >= the requested day count. If insufficient, submission is rejected with a clear error. This check uses the same inclusive day-count formula: requestedDays = (endDate - startDate) + 1. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest sufficiency check appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest in SUBMITTED state is routed to the employee's manager (Employee.managerId). Only that manager (or a user with the ADMIN role) may approve or reject. If the employee has no manager (managerId is null), the request is auto-escalated to any user with ADMIN role. The LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval flag determines whether manager approval is needed at all: if false, the request auto-transitions from SUBMITTED to APPROVED immediately. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Manager approval routing appears, not only here]

When LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays is set (> 0), the LeaveRequest.startDate must be at least minimumNoticeDays calendar days after the submission date (the date the request transitions to SUBMITTED). The notice period is measured as: startDate - submissionDate >= minimumNoticeDays (exclusive of the submission date itself). If violated, submission is rejected. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeavePolicy minimum notice appears, not only here]

Only employees with employmentStatus = 'ACTIVE' may create or submit leave requests. INACTIVE and TERMINATED employees are blocked from new requests. Existing APPROVED requests for a now-TERMINATED employee remain valid; their balances are preserved for audit. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Employee eligibility appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest may only reference a LeaveType where isActive = true. A LeavePolicy referenced by a LeaveBalance must also have isActive = true at the time the balance is created. Deactivating a LeaveType or LeavePolicy does not invalidate existing APPROVED requests or balances. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveType activation appears, not only here]

An employee must not have two LeaveRequests in SUBMITTED or APPROVED state whose date ranges overlap. Overlap is defined as: requestA.startDate <= requestB.endDate AND requestB.startDate <= requestA.endDate. DRAFT and REJECTED requests are excluded from overlap checks. CANCELLED requests are also excluded. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest overlap prevention appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions from SUBMITTED to REJECTED, a rejectionReason must be provided. The rejectedBy and rejectedAt fields are set to the acting manager's ID and the current timestamp respectively. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest rejection appears, not only here]

endDate must be greater than or equal to startDate. A LeaveRequest with endDate < startDate is invalid and must be rejected at creation/submission time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest date validity appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → (APPROVED | REJECTED); any non-terminal state → CANCELLED. REJECTED is terminal (no resubmission — create new request).
- **LeaveType**: ACTIVE | INACTIVE
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE | INACTIVE
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE | CLOSED
- **Employee**: ACTIVE | INACTIVE | TERMINATED (already in DOMAIN.md; confirmed here)
- **Notification**: PENDING | SENT | READ | ARCHIVED (already in DOMAIN.md; extended with leave-specific types)

## Key design decisions

1. **Inclusive day counting** is the foundational semantic: `requestedDays = (endDate - startDate) + 1`. This applies everywhere — sufficiency checks, balance deductions, overlap detection. Recorded as a broad business rule.

2. **pendingDays** on LeaveBalance captures SUBMITTED-but-undecided requests so that the sufficiency check accounts for in-flight requests, preventing double-booking of the same entitlement.

3. **Manager routing** uses Employee.managerId with an ADMIN fallback for managerless employees. LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval can short-circuit to auto-approval.

4. **Balance restoration** on APPROVED → CANCELLED ensures cancelled approved leave returns days to the pool.

5. **Overlap prevention** only considers SUBMITTED and APPROVED requests; DRAFT, REJECTED, and CANCELLED are excluded.

## Open questions for chief architect

- Fiscal year boundary (calendar vs anniversary vs configurable)
- Accrual mechanics (monthly, annual lump-sum, per-pay-period, tenure-based)
- Emergency leave special rules (bypass notice? bypass approval? separate balance pool?)

open_questions.question: How is the fiscal year boundary determined for LeaveBalance? Is it calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), the employee's hire-date anniversary, or a configurable organisation-wide fiscal year start?
open_questions.impact: Determines when new LeaveBalance records are created, when accrual resets, and how year-end carryover is computed. Affects the balance service and any scheduled accrual jobs.
candidate_options: Configurable fiscal year start (e.g. Apr 1) set at organisation level

open_questions.question: How does leave accrual work? LeavePolicy defines accrualRate and maxAccumulation, but the accrual mechanics (frequency, proration for mid-year hires, carryover rules) are not specified.
open_questions.impact: Determines how LeaveBalance.totalEntitlement is computed and when it changes. Affects scheduled jobs, balance service logic, and year-end processing.
candidate_options: Accrual is annual lump-sum at fiscal year start
Accrual is per-pay-period based on accrualRate
Accrual is tenure-based (increases with years of service)

open_questions.question: Does emergency leave have special rules that distinguish it from annual and sick leave? The feature description lists all three but does not specify whether emergency leave bypasses notice periods, approval requirements, or balance checks.
open_questions.impact: Affects the submission validation logic, approval routing, and balance deduction for emergency-type requests. If emergency leave has relaxed rules, the LeavePolicy model may need an `isEmergency` flag or the LeaveType code may drive special-case behaviour.
candidate_options: Emergency leave bypasses minimumNoticeDays and manager approval (auto-approved)
Emergency leave still requires manager approval but bypasses notice period
Emergency leave draws from a separate emergency-specific balance pool
Emergency leave is deducted from annual leave balance but with relaxed rules
